effect_estimate.comment: Exact numeric estimates extracted from Chapter 4 (Tables 4.3, 4.5, and 4.6, PDF pp. 95, 101-102); RQ2 and RQ3 headline results extracted from the Abstract (PDF p. 13) and List of Tables (PDF pp. 9-10), as PDF pp. 104-215 were truncated in the inline text prompt. Note that in Tables 4.5-4.6, Complaint has negative log-odds (-1.270 bivariate; -1.480 multivariate), while text on PDF p. 99 states satisfaction reduced by 72% if the household did not complain compared to those that complained.
effect_estimate.value: Overall, 57.4% of surveyed households (n = 317) were satisfied with the water management committee (Wandiege 81%, Obunga 73.8%, Asengo 58.2%, Paga 16.5%). In multivariate logistic regression for beneficiary satisfaction (n = 317, Nagelkerke R2 = 0.449), 5 of 7 community participation indicators were statistically significant: providing paid/unpaid labor (OR = 2.456, 95% CI: 1.280-4.712, p < 0.05), willingness to intervene against pipe vandalism (OR = 2.627, 95% CI: 1.343-5.139, p < 0.05), attending WATSAN meetings (OR = 2.960, 95% CI: 1.557-5.629, p < 0.05), willingness to contribute money/time for scheme expansion (OR = 1.867, 95% CI: 0.934-3.731, p < 0.10), and complaints about water supply/quality in the past 3 years (OR = 0.228, 95% CI: 0.122-0.425, p < 0.05); paying bills on time (OR = 1.081, 95% CI: 0.370-3.158) and willingness to continue paying on time (OR = 2.243, 95% CI: 0.749-6.717) were non-significant (though all 7 were significant at p < 0.01 in bivariate logit models). Chi-square tests for RQ2 indicate that households using community-managed water schemes and attending water and sanitation meetings tend to practice better water handling hygiene. Qualitative constant comparison analysis (RQ3) identified networking/collaboration, continuous community participation, water consumer groups, coordination/organizational management, institutional formalization, and community dividends as factors aiding scheme performance, while clannism, population increase, poverty, and community fatigue impeded performance.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the MMAT design ceiling. Assigned 2 because the study directly observes and documents community participation and institutional governance mechanisms (elected water management committees, Obunga's Delegated Management Model with KIWASCO under the Water Reform Act of 2002, water consumer groups, meeting participation, complaint handling, tariff collection, and pipe policing) via FGDs, direct meeting observations, archival documents, transect walks, and household survey data.
